canonical_statement: If $G$ is a group then can there exist an exact covering of $G$ by more than one cosets of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one of the cosets)

All endpoint, degeneracy, distinctness, integrality, normalization, and full-sequence conditions required by the canonical statement.

Formal-semantics guard: for this frozen source record the current Lean target signature is exactly `theorem erdos_274 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G],
    1 < ENat.card G → ∀ (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι],

Quantifier-order guard: the quantifiers occur in the order stated and may not be commuted, weakened, or replaced by sampled cases. Salient source phrases include: there exist an exact covering of $G$ by more than one cosets of different sizes.
Threshold guard: every “at most/at least/more than/less than” boundary is literal; strict and non-strict inequalities and integer rounding may not be interchanged.

Review-authority rule for this repaired contract: the immutable canonical_statement is the controlling mathematical target. Where a reviewer defect identifies an exact source/Lean encoding as the intended convention, that exact encoding is binding; any alternative convention mentioned only to expose ambiguity is forbidden unless exact equivalence to the controlling target is proved.

Binding semantic repair: definitions: the second open declaration `herzog_schonheim` in the frozen source (index version: ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ (P.parts i).index = (P.parts j).index) is not pinned anywhere. The known_traps entry 'MULTI-FORMAL-TARGET TRAP' flags 2 open declarations, but the contract never states whether the index-form and cardinality-form are co-targets or whether one close suffices; an attacker could close only the cardinality form (or only the index form) and claim completion.

Binding semantic repair: definitions: the key predicate `Group.ExactCovering` (nonempty parts, pairwise disjoint cosets `reps i • parts i`, union = univ) is load-bearing but never defined in the contract; a reformulation could swap 'exact covering' for a mere covering (dropping disjointness) or a partition of the subgroup lattice, silently changing the claim. The nonemptiness clause and the pointwise-smul coset convention are unprotected.

Binding semantic repair: definitions: the hypotheses `1 < ENat.card G` (G nontrivial, via ENat cardinality, allowing infinite G) and `1 < Fintype.card ι` (more than one coset) are threshold conditions on different cardinality notions (ENat.card vs Fintype.card); no guard prevents conflating them or restricting to finite G, which would be a domain drift the non_results list does not name for this problem.

Every quantifier, domain, hypothesis, strict/non-strict inequality, endpoint, normalization, and parameter dependency survives every reformulation.
Discrete structure is preserved: integrality, distinctness, ordering, multiplicity/set-vs-multiset conventions, and exact cardinalities may not be relaxed silently.
Any asymptotic/eventual claim retains the same limiting variable and full-sequence requirement.
The frozen current Lean signature remains semantically consistent with the prose contract; binder types and predicates may not be altered merely to make the theorem easier to prove.
known_traps: QUANTIFIER SLIP: exchanging ∀ and ∃, moving an epsilon/constant after the limiting variable, or replacing “all sufficiently large” by “infinitely many”.
SAMPLED-TO-UNIVERSAL: checking many finite instances and promoting the observation to an unrestricted theorem without a valid finite-reduction theorem.
DOMAIN DRIFT: proving a translated/scaled/relaxed version without an exact map back to the original domain, endpoints, and discrete constraints.
STRENGTH CONFUSION: refuting a stronger folklore conjecture does not refute the canonical claim; proving a weaker statement does not prove it.

FORMAL/PROSE DRIFT: a Lean proof is acceptable only if the exact frozen signature is semantically the same target. `answer(sorry)` or independently filled answer metavariables are not permission to choose an easier proposition/function.
